## 1. EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

### 1.1 What It Is

A complete architectural Blueprint for implementing a User Management Module in a SaaS MVP, covering authentication, authorization, profile management, and multi-tenancy foundations.

### 1.2 Why It Exists

**Job To Be Done:**

> "When starting a new SaaS MVP, I want a well-architected user management foundation, so that I don't accumulate technical debt in the most critical module of my application."

### 1.3 Expected Deliverables

- [ ] Authentication system (email/password + OAuth2)
- [ ] Role-based authorization (RBAC)
- [ ] User profile management
- [ ] Multi-tenant data isolation
- [ ] Security best practices implemented
- [ ] Complete test coverage

      - Security vulnerabilities

  WHERE:

    deadline: "Before any other feature development"

  HOW:
    constraints:

#### EPIC 1: Schema Design

**Objective:** Define all data structures before writing code

**Stories:**

**S-1.1: Database Schema Design**

| Task | Description | Criteria | Duration |
|------|-------------|----------|----------|
| T-1.1.1 | Create User table schema | Table exists with all fields | 30min |
| T-1.1.2 | Create Tenant table schema | Multi-tenant structure defined | 30min |
| T-1.1.3 | Create Role and Permission tables | RBAC tables defined | 30min |
| T-1.1.4 | Create AuditLog table | Security events can be stored | 20min |
| T-1.1.5 | Define relationships and indexes | Foreign keys, indexes created | 30min |

**S-1.2: TypeScript Types**

| Task | Description | Criteria | Duration |
|------|-------------|----------|----------|
| T-1.2.1 | Define User entity types | Types compile without errors | 20min |
| T-1.2.2 | Define Auth DTOs | Request/Response types defined | 20min |
| T-1.2.3 | Define Permission enums | All roles/permissions enumerated | 15min |

**Checkpoint CP-1:** Schema validated, types compile, ready for implementation

### 6.1 Prerequisites

Before starting:

- [ ] PostgreSQL database available
- [ ] S3-compatible storage configured
- [ ] Google OAuth2 credentials obtained
- [ ] Email service configured
- [ ] Environment variables set

### 6.2 First Steps

1. Run database migrations (T-1.1.x tasks)
2. Verify types compile (T-1.2.x tasks)
3. Begin with registration endpoint (T-2.1.3)

### 6.3 Decision Points

| After | Decision | Options |
|-------|----------|---------|
| PH-2 | Session strategy | JWT-only vs JWT+Refresh |
| PH-3 | Permission model | Role-based vs Permission-based |
| PH-5 | Rate limit strategy | Per-IP vs Per-user |

## APPENDICES

### A. Database Schema

```sql
-- Users table
CREATE TABLE users (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  tenant_id UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES tenants(id),
  email VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  password_hash VARCHAR(255),
  google_id VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE,
  email_verified BOOLEAN DEFAULT FALSE,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW(),
  updated_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Tenants table
CREATE TABLE tenants (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(255) NOT NULL,
  slug VARCHAR(255) UNIQUE NOT NULL,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);

-- Roles table
CREATE TABLE roles (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  name VARCHAR(50) NOT NULL,
  permissions JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'
);

-- User Roles junction
CREATE TABLE user_roles (
  user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  role_id UUID REFERENCES roles(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  PRIMARY KEY (user_id, role_id)
);

-- Audit Log
CREATE TABLE audit_logs (
  id UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),
  user_id UUID REFERENCES users(id),
  action VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  metadata JSONB DEFAULT '{}',
  ip_address INET,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT NOW()
);
```
